artworks.title: Deucalion and Pyrrha
artworks.description: A Baroque painting of the flood survivors on the heights of Parnassus, when the waters had receded and Themis' oracle bade them cast the bones of their mother — the stones of Earth — behind their shoulders to refather mankind. The scene condenses Apollodorus 1.7.2 and Ovid Metamorphoses 1.348–415 into the image that became the standard visual shorthand for the Greek deluge.

artworks.title: The Flood
artworks.description: Girodet's neoclassical canvas treats the Ovidian catastrophe in universal terms: a family clings to a rock as the Bronze-Age world dissolves beneath the rains Jupiter loosed after Lycaon's impiety. Though not Deucalion-specific, it captures the moral cosmology of the great flood shelf — divine wrath against a wicked race, with only the just spared.
